growth-health.title: Growth health
growth-health.what_to_watch: Whether acquisition is producing healthy, qualified growth rather than merely more traffic.
growth-health.why_watch: Leadership wants to know when growth performance needs coordinated action across marketing, product, and sales.
watch_for: The qualified acquisition outcome is moving materially relative to its normal baseline.
A related funnel, product, or campaign signal helps explain whether the movement matters.
Data freshness and comparability are sufficient for an operating decision.
questions: Is this a meaningful change in the growth outcome or an expected operating pattern?
Which connected signal best explains what the growth team should do next?

fulfillment-reliability.title: Fulfillment reliability
fulfillment-reliability.what_to_watch: Whether customer delivery promises remain reliable across the order, warehouse, and carrier flow.
fulfillment-reliability.why_watch: Operations needs early warning when a delivery problem is broad enough to require intervention, not every isolated late package.
watch_for: The delivery promise is materially off course across more than one operational signal.
Warehouse, carrier, or inventory evidence identifies a plausible source of the movement.
The source data is complete enough to distinguish a real service problem from a reporting gap.
questions: Is the customer-facing delivery risk broad enough to act on now?
Is the strongest explanation in warehouse capacity, carrier performance, or inventory availability?

payment-trust.title: Payment trust
payment-trust.what_to_watch: Whether customers can complete payment reliably without introducing fraud or compliance exposure.
payment-trust.why_watch: Risk and payments leaders need one view of revenue loss, issuer behavior, fraud pressure, and control health.
watch_for: Payment completion or loss is moving materially across a meaningful customer population.
Issuer, fraud, or control signals distinguish a recoverable payment issue from a risk event.
Authorization and data-quality evidence are trustworthy before action is taken.
questions: Should the payments team intervene, investigate, or leave the movement alone?
What connected evidence best explains the change without overstating causation?

customer-retention.title: Customer retention
customer-retention.what_to_watch: Whether important customer relationships are becoming less healthy in a way that needs coordinated response.
customer-retention.why_watch: Executives care about durable retention risk, not normal account-level noise or a single delayed renewal.
watch_for: Retention risk is visible in both customer behavior and commercial signals.
Support, product usage, or account context helps distinguish a real relationship risk.
The account and revenue sources use comparable definitions and current data.
questions: Is the retention signal broad and important enough for leadership attention?
Which customer-facing signal should the account team investigate first?

product-adoption.title: Product adoption
product-adoption.what_to_watch: Whether newly released product capabilities are reaching the intended users and creating healthy usage.
product-adoption.why_watch: Product leadership needs to separate real adoption problems from planned rollout effects, instrumentation gaps, and normal cohort variation.
watch_for: Adoption is materially different from the expected rollout path.
Usage, experiment, and release evidence agree on whether the movement is meaningful.
Instrumentation or data freshness problems are not being mistaken for product behavior.
questions: Is this an adoption problem, a rollout effect, or an instrumentation problem?
What should the product team inspect before changing the plan?

cloud-reliability.title: Cloud reliability
cloud-reliability.what_to_watch: Whether the platform can support customer workloads reliably and whether incidents need coordinated response.
cloud-reliability.why_watch: Platform leaders need signal across service health, deploys, incidents, and capacity instead of manually checking each system.
watch_for: Customer-impacting reliability is meaningfully worse than the operating baseline.
A deploy, incident, or capacity signal supports a plausible explanation.
The monitoring and incident data is fresh and complete enough to act.
questions: Is there a customer-impacting platform issue that needs escalation?
What operational evidence should the on-call team inspect first?

delivery-promise.title: Delivery promise
delivery-promise.what_to_watch: Whether delivery performance is still aligned with the promise made to customers and with available fleet capacity.
delivery-promise.why_watch: The operations team should act on a system-level service risk, not chase normal variation in individual routes.
watch_for: Customer delivery performance and route capacity indicate a broad service risk.
Carrier, weather, or warehouse context explains or contradicts the movement.
The operational data is current and comparable across regions.
questions: Is the delivery promise at risk across the network or only in one pocket?
Which operational owner should investigate first?

fleet-cost.title: Fleet cost control
fleet-cost.what_to_watch: Whether transportation cost is drifting for reasons the business can act on without reducing service quality.
fleet-cost.why_watch: Finance and operations need to connect cost movement to fuel, utilization, route mix, and customer service rather than react to a single number.
watch_for: Cost is materially off plan and the movement is not explained by an expected route or fuel effect.
Utilization, fuel, or service evidence identifies a likely operational driver.
The cost and service views use the same period and population.
questions: Is the cost movement actionable without creating a service problem?
What connected operating signal should the team use to choose a response?

care-operations.title: Care operations
care-operations.what_to_watch: Whether access to care is deteriorating in a way that needs operational intervention while quality remains protected.
care-operations.why_watch: Care leaders need a joined view of demand, wait time, staffing, quality, and incident context.
watch_for: Access or wait-time performance is materially worse across the relevant care population.
Staffing, demand, or quality evidence explains whether the movement requires action.
Patient and operational data are complete and trustworthy enough to discuss.
questions: Is this a real access problem or a data and scheduling artifact?
Which care-operations owner should respond first?

revenue-cycle.title: Revenue cycle
revenue-cycle.what_to_watch: Whether revenue collection is on course and whether operational friction is creating avoidable financial risk.
revenue-cycle.why_watch: Finance leadership needs to connect cash movement to claims, denials, payment timing, and source trust.
watch_for: Cash or collection performance is materially off course relative to the operating plan.
Claims, denials, or payment timing provide a connected explanation.
The source definitions and data freshness support a responsible escalation.
questions: Is the financial movement actionable now or does it require investigation first?
Which operational evidence best explains the collection gap?

production-quality.title: Production quality
production-quality.what_to_watch: Whether production quality is drifting in a way that creates customer, safety, or cost consequences.
production-quality.why_watch: Plant and quality leaders need connected evidence across yield, defects, maintenance, and release holds.
watch_for: Quality performance is materially outside the normal operating range.
Maintenance, material, or process evidence supports a likely explanation.
Inspection coverage and source freshness are sufficient before escalation.
questions: Is this a plant-level quality issue or an isolated measurement problem?
What evidence should the quality owner investigate before changing production?

supply-continuity.title: Supply continuity
supply-continuity.what_to_watch: Whether critical supply inputs are at risk of disrupting production or customer commitments.
supply-continuity.why_watch: Supply leaders need to connect inventory, supplier performance, purchase orders, and demand changes before a shortage becomes an outage.
watch_for: Critical supply coverage is materially below the expected operating position.
Supplier, demand, or purchase-order evidence distinguishes a real risk from a planning artifact.
Inventory and supplier data are fresh and comparable.
questions: Is there a supply risk that needs intervention before the next planning cycle?
Which supplier or demand signal should the operating team investigate first?
